Supported models of table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_models.R
table_regression_models.Rd

table_regression_models() returns the registry of model classes supported by table_regression(), one row per engine, with each class's family, average-marginal-effects estimand, exponentiate semantics, labeled table blocks, accepted vcov values and fit statistics. The same registry drives the table of this page and those of the family pages, so the published list cannot drift from the code.

This page is the overview: the table of every supported class, the rules all classes share, and the page of each family, which gives its arguments, the values the shared arguments take for it, and what it refuses.

If a class is not listed: fit the model and call table_regression(fit) anyway – unsupported classes error with a clear message naming the supported set. Feature requests are welcome on the issue tracker.

A class listed here does not cover the objects that inherit from it without being that model. These are refused by name: clogit, multi-state coxph, coxph with a pspline() or a non-sparse frailty() term, svysurvreg, mlm (an lm() with a matrix response), aov, nlme, gnls, the lme and gam parts of a mgcv::gamm() fit, and the rms::Rq() and rms::Gls() wrappers.

Usage

table_regression_models()

Value

A data frame with one row per supported engine and columns family, class, engine, ame, exponentiate, blocks, vcov (the values of vcov the class accepts), fit_stats_default (the fit-statistic rows of a one-model table under the default show_fit_stats, in their order) and fit_stats (the tokens of show_fit_stats that give a row for one model; the change tokens, which need nested = TRUE, are not listed). A parenthesis in a cell gives the fits an item is limited to.

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available, and what they estimate (per category for ordinal models, per outcome for multinomial models, yes (draws) for Bayesian fits). Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts; see Robust SE availability by model class in table_regression().

Pages by model family

  • table_regression_mixed: lmer, glmer, glmmTMB, lme and gls fits.

  • table_regression_survival: coxph, survreg, cph and flexsurvreg fits.

  • table_regression_ordinal: polr, clm and clmm fits.

  • table_regression_categorical: multinom and mlogit fits.

  • table_regression_counts: zeroinfl and hurdle fits, and the zero-inflation, hurdle and dispersion blocks of glmmTMB.

  • table_regression_survey: svyglm, svyolr and svycoxph fits.

  • table_regression_bayesian: stanreg and brmsfit fits.

  • table_regression_robust: lm_robust, iv_robust, ivreg, tobit, rq and fixest fits.

The linear and generalized linear models are documented on table_regression() itself. GEE fits are described below. The additive, beta-regression, sample-selection and rms fits follow the rules of table_regression() and the table above. The tokens of show_columns and show_fit_stats, and the fit statistics of each class, are on table_regression_tokens.

A sample-selection fit (sampleSelection::selection(), heckit(), treatReg()) shows each variable with its selection and outcome sub-rows, then an Error terms block: \(\sigma\) and \(\rho\) for a maximum-likelihood fit (\(\rho\) alone for a binary outcome), the inverse Mills ratio \(\lambda\) followed by \(\sigma\) and \(\rho\) without standard errors for a two-step fit. Tests and intervals use the t distribution with the residual df that summary() uses. The note names the standard errors, "classical (Fisher information)" for a maximum-likelihood fit and "classical (two-step)" for a two-step fit, and the number of cases with an observed outcome. A tobit-5 (switching regression) fit is refused.

Shared semantics (all classes)

  • A robust vcov request is honored through the class's backend, or refused with an error that names the supported set; the footer names the estimator applied.

  • exponentiate = TRUE is link-gated: it produces a labeled ratio (OR / IRR / HR / RR / MR / TR) only where the link warrants one. Identity-link fits warn and are left untouched; non-ratio links (probit, cauchit, inverse, ...) are refused with an error.

  • Class-specific structure renders as labeled subordinate blocks of rows in the same table, each explained by a footer line.

  • Fit statistics default to the family's field standard (show_fit_stats overrides; class-inappropriate tokens are rejected with a pointer to the right ones).

  • Everything is available programmatically: broom::tidy(), glance(), as_structured(), as.data.frame().

Population-averaged (GEE) models

geepack::geeglm() fits are read on their own terms: the sandwich standard errors the fit computed (its std.err = option, clustered on its id =) are the displayed inference – GEE is robust by construction, so spicy's HC* and CR* tokens, the resamplers and cluster are refused with a pointer to the fit options. Coefficients are population-averaged (marginal) effects; the footer discloses the working correlation structure with its estimated alpha. Wald z inference; exponentiate follows the usual link gates (OR / IRR / RR). Default fit statistics report the cluster structure (n, N (<id>), largest cluster); the quasi-likelihood information criteria "qic" / "qicu" (Pan 2001) and the "scale" (dispersion) parameter are opt-in – there is no likelihood, so AIC, pseudo-R-squared, nested = TRUE, and standardized are refused. See the GEE regression tables article, and the population-averaged section of the Mixed-effects regression tables article for the contrast with subject-specific mixed models.

References

Pan, W. (2001). Akaike's information criterion in generalized estimating equations. Biometrics, 57(1), 120-125. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2001.00120.x

See also

table_regression(); the family pages listed under Pages by model family; table_regression_tokens for the tokens of show_columns and show_fit_stats; the Supported models and Publication-ready regression tables articles.
